fills.reason: The only WebView config sets javaScriptEnabled=true and leaves allowContentAccess at its default, but never enables setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs (default false), so the fail condition (all three) is not met.

JavaScript is enabled and allowFileAccess keeps its default, but neither setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs nor setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs is set (both default false with minSdk 23), so the third condition is not met.

Every credential field (HTTP auth password, Improv Wi-Fi password, mTLS certificate password) uses KeyboardType.Password with PasswordVisualTransformation; XML EditTexts are widget labels/URLs, not sensitive.

No FLAG_SECURE / setRecentsScreenshotEnabled anywhere in the app. Whether the HA dashboard (camera feeds, home state) and the HTTP-auth dialog count as sensitive enough to need screenshot protection is a product decision.

App-generated notifications contain only generic strings; server-pushed notifications carry user-authored automation text and default to VISIBILITY_PRIVATE unless the user sets 'public'; the high-accuracy location notification is VISIBILITY_SECRET.
Password fields are masked with PasswordVisualTransformation by default; they only reveal on an explicit user toggle.

JS is enabled and the legacy V1 bridge (addJavascriptInterface 'externalApp', used for servers older than 2026.4.2) exposes getExternalAuth/externalBus with no origin or frame check, unlike V2. Top-level navigation is limited to the server origin, but the interface is injected into every frame, including user-configured third-party iframes on dashboards. Whether that iframe reach is acceptable needs a human threat-model decision.

The app has login (HTTP auth credentials) and security-settings UI (app lock) but uses no overlay protection anywhere: no filterTouchesWhenObscured, onFilterTouchEventForSecurity, FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED check or setHideOverlayWindows.

evidence.detail: Credential entry field with no touch-filtering protection.

fills.reason: Every internal sendBroadcast uses an explicit component (Intent(context, X::class.java)) or setPackage(packageName); the only package-less broadcast is the user-configured command in MessagingManager, which is meant for external apps.
Intents carrying extras (widget ids, sensor ids, entity ids, location commands) are explicit or package-scoped; no implicit intent carries tokens or credentials.

With minSdk 23, several PendingIntents for plain notification actions and device controls are created with FLAG_MUTABLE, although nothing needs to fill them in (location/activity-recognition and widget-config ones have a valid need).

evidence.detail: Notification 'disable' action PendingIntent is mutable without need.

homeassistant:// handlers validate the host against an allowlist, convert server_id with toIntOrNull, re-encode paths, and load only targets with the same origin as the server (others open externally); the invite and wear-sign-in URLs only prefill a user-driven onboarding flow.

fills.reason: Read the key exported activities. LinkActivity validates its input; WidgetAuthenticationActivity requires device auth. But ShareActivity lets any app silently fire a 'mobile_app.share' event with attacker text to the user's server (it can trigger automations), and AssistActivity, exported without a permission, shows over the keyguard and takes server/pipeline from extras. Whether these are intended capabilities is a product decision.

Wearable listeners (WearOnboardingListener, WearDnsRequestListener, PhoneSettingsListener) are only delivered by Play services from paired nodes, and HaCarAppService uses a HostValidator allowlist in release. MatterCommissioningService returns its binder to any caller and relies on unverified GMS-side signature checks (per the manifest comment), which can't be confirmed from code.

TemplateWidget is exported only to get boot broadcasts, yet its onReceive accepts ACTION_APPWIDGET_CREATED from any caller and writes an attacker-supplied serialized TemplateWidgetEntity (a template the server renders with the user's token) into the DB for any widget id.

evidence.detail: TemplateWidget receiver declared exported with no permission.
Intent-supplied widget entity is persisted without checking the caller.

fills.reason: No java.util.Random, kotlin.random or Math.random in non-test code; identifiers (install id, NFC tag id, BLE UUID, shortcut ids) use UUID.randomUUID (SecureRandom-backed).
Security-relevant identifiers are created with UUID.randomUUID; tokens come from the server. No time-based values (Date().time, Calendar.MILLISECOND) are used as secrets.
No KeyGenerator or KeyPairGenerator in app code; the only keys are imported mTLS client certificates.
No Cipher, SecretKeyFactory or KeyGenerator usage anywhere in app code.
No Cipher.getInstance calls in app code, so no block cipher mode is chosen.
No KeyGenParameterSpec / KeyPairGenerator: the app generates no asymmetric keys (it only imports an mTLS key into AndroidKeyStore).
getInstance calls name no provider: KeyStore uses "AndroidKeyStore" or the type "PKCS12", SSLContext uses "TLS", and TrustManagerFactory uses the default algorithm.
The app calls KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure/isKeyguardSecure and BiometricManager.canAuthenticate before offering app lock.
The app lock and authenticated widget/notification actions (which can control the home) use BiometricPrompt with DEVICE_CREDENTIAL allowed alongside BIOMETRIC_WEAK.

evidence.detail: Allowed authenticators include device credential fallback and weak biometrics.

fills.reason: App lock and authenticated widget actions rely only on onAuthenticationSucceeded: authenticate() is called without a CryptoObject, and no key is created with setUserAuthenticationRequired.

evidence.detail: Event-bound BiometricPrompt call without a CryptoObject.

fills.reason: No KeyGenParameterSpec or setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment anywhere; biometrics are not bound to keys.

setConfirmationRequired(false) is used for the single Authenticator that gates the app lock and 'require authentication' widget/notification actions (e.g. door controls), which are sensitive operations needing explicit authorization.

evidence.detail: Passive biometrics accepted without explicit user confirmation.

fills.reason: No keys are generated with setUserAuthenticationParameters or setUserAuthenticationValidityDurationSeconds; biometrics are not crypto-bound.
The OkHttp setup uses SSLContext "TLS" with platform defaults; there is no ConnectionSpec, tlsVersions, setEnabledProtocols or TLSv1/1.1 anywhere.

Hardcoded http:// strings in Kotlin are UI placeholders and Compose previews (homeassistant.local, my.homeassistant.io in @HAPreviews); server URLs are user-supplied. Cleartext permission itself is covered by MASTG-TEST-0235.
No direct SSLSocket use; all TLS goes through OkHttp (default hostname verifier) or WebView.

A custom X509ExtendedTrustManager is installed in OkHttp that, when platform validation fails, retries against a trust manager built from user-installed CAs. This explicitly loosens trust and duplicates what the NSC already allows.

evidence.detail: Rejected server chains are retried against the user-CA fallback.
User-installed CA trust manager wired into the handshake.

fills.reason: No custom HostnameVerifier or hostnameVerifier() override exists; OkHttp's default verifier is used.
onReceivedSslError calls super (which cancels) and then shows an error; proceed() is never called on an SslErrorHandler.
ProviderInstaller.installIfNeeded/installIfNeededAsync is never called before the TLS stack is set up (minSdk 23).

evidence.detail: TLS context created without updating the GMS security provider first.

The only first-party native lib (microwakeword) is built by CMake with NDK clang, which emits PIE by default; no -no-pie/-fno-pic flags. Prebuilt .so files from dependencies were not inspected.
CMake flags add -O3/-ffast-math only; no -fno-stack-protector, so NDK clang's default -fstack-protector-strong applies. Prebuilt .so files from dependencies were not inspected.
The app checks the OS version throughout via SdkVersion.isAtLeast(Build.VERSION_CODES.*).
Needs an SBOM (CycloneDX) generated from a Gradle build and run through a dependency tracker; Ward's direct-dependency scan is reported under MASTG-TEST-0272.

The only data-handling SDK call is SentryAndroid.init (crash reports, session tracking, breadcrumbs), gated by a user opt-in and with user data stripped to the id in beforeSend; FCM is used for push tokens. Whether this matches the Data safety declaration needs a human.
